newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF will not have Euro allies in 1st phase.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF will not have Euro allies in 1st phase.

text.p: France will seek European allies for Thomson-CSF but only after carrying out a French restructuring for the defence firm whose privatisation it halted last week, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn was quoted in parliamentary minutes as saying on Wednesday.

Strauss-Kahn told a closed meeting of the parliamentary defence panel the Socialist-led government envisaged bringing in a French partner first, by lowering its 58 percent stake to less than 50 percent, then looking for European alliances. It had previously been unclear if the government would go directly for a Europe-wide restructuring needed to tackle U.S. competition.

Paraphrasing Strauss-Kahn's remarks, the minutes said: "He would like Thomson to be allowed to group together with French companies first -- that is, to find a large industrial partner -- while at the same time the state's share falls beneath 50 percent. Then, at a second stage, it would make alliances with European partners which have an interest in doing so."

Strauss-Kahn was quoted as telling the committee that the government, which has vowed to keep a "decisive" public stake in Thomson-CSF, had not decided how this involvement should be structured. It could, he said, be in the form of a direct capital stake, a golden share or a pact with other shareholders.
French newspapers have reported widely that the government wants to bring an outsider into Thomson-CSF either directly, through extra capital, or through a new joint-owned entity.

Press reports favour engineering firm Alcatel Alsthom to win a key role in a restructured Thomson-CSF along with its partner Dassault. Alcatel's rival for Thomson-CSF, missile maker Lagardere which teamed up with Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa), has dismissed the reports however as premature.

Others interested in alliances with Thomson-CSF include British giant General Electric's defence division GEC-Marconi. Its chairman Geoffrey Pattie said in Paris on Wednesday he hoped for a quick decision on Thomson-CSF's fate.
